body.title: [Gitlab-ci] Release error in CI/CD
body.description:

Please read this!

- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/issues/?label_name%5B%5D=type%3A%3Abug

and verify the issue you're about to submit isn't a duplicate.
--->

### Checklist

<!-- Please test the latest versions, that will remove the possibility that you see a bug that is fixed in a newer version. -->

- [X] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`)
  - Extension version: _Put your extension version here_
- [X] Operating system and version: Docker image `registry.gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli:latest`
- [X] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? Self managed instance
- [X] GitLab version (if self-managed) 18.6.2 (`gitlab/gitlab-ce:18.6.2-ce.0`)
  (Use the `version` endpoint, like this: gitlab.my-company.com/api/v4/version) 
- [ ] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues
- [ ] Run the command in debug mode (like `DEBUG=true glab mr list`) and attach any useful output

### Summary

<!-- Summarize the bug encountered concisely -->

I use the docker image at `registry.gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli:latest` to run my release job, however I keep getting error.

### Environment

As mentioned earlier, I'm running a self-hosted Gitlab Community Docker instance (`gitlab/gitlab-ce:18.6.2-ce.0`), using a runner with Docker executor (other jobs with docker run ok).

My Gitlab instance is behind a reverse proxy (using Nginx Proxy Manager) for both Gitlab and Gitlab registry (`gitlab.my-domain-name` and `registry.my-domain-name` respectively).

Here is my omnibus config for gitlab:
```yaml
      GITLAB_OMNIBUS_CONFIG: |
        registry_external_url "${EXTERNAL_URL}"
        gitlab_rails['gitlab_shell_ssh_port'] = "${HOST_SSH_PORT}"
        nginx['listen_port'] = "${CONTAINER_HTTP_PORT}"
        nginx['listen_https'] = false
        registry_nginx['listen_port'] = "${CONTAINER_REGISTRY_PORT}"
        registry_nginx['listen_https'] = false
        registry_nginx['proxy_http_version'] = 1.1
        registry_nginx['proxy_set_headers'] = {
          "X-Forwarded-Proto" => "https",
          "X-Forwarded-Ssl" => "on"
        }
        gitlab_rails['smtp_enable'] = true
        gitlab_rails['smtp_address'] = "smtp.gmail.com"
        gitlab_rails['smtp_port'] = 587
        gitlab_rails['smtp_user_name'] = "${USERNAME}"
        gitlab_rails['smtp_password'] = "${PASSWORD}"
        gitlab_rails['smtp_domain'] = "smtp.gmail.com"
        gitlab_rails['smtp_authentication'] = "login"
        gitlab_rails['smtp_enable_starttls_auto'] = true
        gitlab_rails['smtp_tls'] = false
        gitlab_rails['smtp_openssl_verify_mode'] = 'peer'
```

<details>
<summary>
Though I haven't done any particular config on my external Nginx, here is my setup
</summary>
![image](/uploads/c8fee8d1b8484e1d80c1aec1d9c4dc72/image.png){width=495 height=544}
![image](/uploads/433185104faca004f375f32bdf65d5c3/image.png){width=395 height=600}
![image](/uploads/bfe11a026aff29be66efd0be06afac8f/image.png){width=498 height=381}
![image](/uploads/f827959e4d10e579878f463a6b81ad8e/image.png){width=498 height=599}
</details>

<!--
Please include any other information that you believe might be relevant
in debugging. For example, you may include a shell framework like oh-my-zsh
or other customizations like editing the prompt (PS1, PS2, and others).
-->

### Steps to reproduce

<!-- How one can reproduce the issue - this is very important -->

Both build and package jobs run successfully, and package registry has the file. Here is my release job:

```yaml
release:
  stage: release
  image: registry.gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli:latest
  rules:
    - if: ${CI_COMMIT_TAG}
  script:
    - echo "Running the release job."
  release:
    tag_name: ${CI_COMMIT_TAG}
    name: 'Release ${CI_COMMIT_TAG}'
    description: "Release ${CI_COMMIT_TAG} at ${CI_API_V4_URL}/projects/${CI_PROJECT_ID}/packages/generic/${PACKAGE_NAME}/${CI_COMMIT_TAG}/${PACKAGE_NAME}.exe"
```
Note that I first ran with assets instead of linking the package in the description, but that fails as well.

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

The release job fails, no release created.

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

The release job should be successful and the release is created.

### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

I got the following error:
```
Executing "step_script" stage of the job script 00:00
Using docker image sha256:54b05805f30401108ba5c40adfb1f056e7733554874958c3cabfa219b69db8e7 for registry.gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli:latest with digest registry.gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli@sha256:3015164b5a7d16288d3ac7c48d6685e30071603b3b519a8fb3cc177ba22ef40f ...
$ echo "Running the release job."
Running the release job.
Executing "step_release" stage of the job script 00:02
$ if command -v glab &> /dev/null; then # collapsed multi-line command
• Creating or updating release repo=###/############# tag=########
          
   ERROR  
          
  Json: cannot unmarshal array into Go value of type gitlab.Release.                                                  
Cleaning up project directory and file based variables 00:01
ERROR: Job failed: exit code 1
```
I saw this behaviour similar to another issue in `release-cli`, but I don't know if it is related to my Nginx: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/release-cli/-/issues?sort=created_date&state=closed&search=cannot+unmarshal&first_page_size=20&show=eyJpaWQiOiIxMzYiLCJmdWxsX3BhdGgiOiJnaXRsYWItb3JnL3JlbGVhc2UtY2xpIiwiaWQiOjEwMDM4MzAzMX0%3D

I can't seem to see any workaround on that issue, however. Using `release-cli` also creates a similar bug.

### Possible fixes

body.title: `host` config key / GITLAB_HOST overrides repo remotes instead of acting as a fallback
body.description:
### Checklist

- [x] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`)
  - Extension version: glab 1.120.0 (78790114c)
  - Also reproduced from source at main (`glab DEV`)
- [x] Operating system and version: Linux 7.2.8-200.fc44.x86_64 x86_64
- [x] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? _both_
- [x] GitLab version (if self-managed) _v19.3.3_
- [x] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues
- [x] Run the command in debug mode (like `GLAB_DEBUG=true glab mr list`) and attach any useful output

### Summary

The top-level `host:` key in `config.yml` (or the `GITLAB_HOST` / `GITLAB_URI` / `GL_HOST` environment variables) is treated as an **override when inside a Git repository** instead of as a default for when no host can be resolved. When the key differs from the repo's remote host, glab filters the remotes down to the configured host and fails all repo-bound commands. The key is documented as "Default GitLab instance, outside Git repositories", so it should only apply when the remote (or a URL argument) doesn't determine the host.

### Environment

- OS: Linux 7.2.8-200.fc44.x86_64 x86_64
- SHELL: /bin/bash
- TERM: xterm-256color
- GLAB: glab 1.120.0 (78790114c)

### Steps to reproduce

With no network required (the failure happens before any API call):

```sh
git init /tmp/repro && cd /tmp/repro
git remote add origin https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli.git
mkdir -p /tmp/cfg && cat > /tmp/cfg/config.yml <<'EOF'
git_protocol: https
host: gitlab.tuwien.ac.at
hosts:
  gitlab.tuwien.ac.at:
    token: fake
    api_protocol: https
    git_protocol: https
EOF
chmod 600 /tmp/cfg/config.yml
GLAB_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/cfg glab issue list
```

Setting `host:` to anything other than `gitlab.com` (or setting `GITLAB_HOST`) triggers the filter in any repo whose remote points to a different instance.

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

1. The command fails with `None of the git remotes configured for this repository correspond to the GITLAB_HOST environment variable` even when **no** environment variable is set and the value came from the `host:` key — the error message is misleading.
2. With `-R OWNER/REPO` (no host in the argument), the request silently goes to the configured instance instead of the repo's remote host, targeting the wrong instance and token.

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

- Inside a Git repository, the remote (or a URL argument) determines the host; the `host:` key / `GITLAB_HOST` are only fallbacks when the host cannot be resolved (e.g. outside a repo).
- The error message should say which source set the override (config key vs. env var).

### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

```
$ GLAB_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/cfg GLAB_DEBUG=true glab issue list
2026/10/08 19:04:51 [Could not determine base repo in telemetry hook:  none of the git remotes
configured for this repository correspond to the GITLAB_HOST environment variable. Try adding
a matching remote or unsetting the variable.

GITLAB_HOST is currently set to gitlab.tuwien.ac.at

Configured remotes: gitlab.com]

   ERROR

  None of the git remotes configured for this repository correspond to the GITLAB_HOST
  environment variable. Try adding a matching remote or unsetting the variable.

  GITLAB_HOST is currently set to gitlab.tuwien.ac.at

  Configured remotes: gitlab.com.
```

(Note: in the debug log line, the trailing `]` closes the `GLAB_DEBUG` log entry, which wraps the message in brackets; it is not part of the error text.)

### Possible fixes

- `internal/cmdutils/factory.go`: `defaultHostname` is set from `cfg.Get("", "host")` before `BaseRepo()` resolves; `Remotes()` then sets `hostOverride` whenever the default differs from `gitlab.com` (\~line 192).
- `internal/cmdutils/remote_resolver.go`: the `hostOverride` block (\~lines 103-127) drops all non-matching remotes, then errors out.
- `RepoOverride` (`factory.go`) resolves `-R OWNER/REPO` against `defaultHostname` instead of the repo's remote host.
- Note: `remote_resolver_test.go` (\~line 428) locks in the current override behavior, so this needs a decision on intended semantics (env var as hard override vs. fallback), not just a test change.
- Related: #8084 covers the URL-host case of the same host-resolution model.

body.title: Impossible to configure_docker, since container_registry_domains is not stored when --use-keyring is supplied and also not checked
body.description:
### Checklist

<!-- Please test the latest versions, that will remove the possibility that you see a bug that is fixed in a newer version. -->

- [x] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`)
  - Extension version: 1.65.0
- [x] Operating system and version: Fedora 42
- [x] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? self-managed instance
- [x] GitLab version (if self-managed) 18.05
- [x] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues
- [ ] Run the command in debug mode (like `DEBUG=true glab mr list`) and attach any useful output

### Summary

Using `glab auth login` with `--use-keyring` does not store the survey answer to supplied container registry domains.

Additionally `glab auth status` does not check for validity of container registry credentials.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Login with `glab auth login --use-keyring` and provide container registry domains
2. Try to do `glab auth configure-docker`
3. See the error

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

The error is thrown:

```
ERROR: no hosts were configured - ensure you've logged in via oauth2 and configured at least one container registry domain for a host
```

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

`configure_docker` succeeds and container registry domains are retained when using the keyring, as without using `--use-keyring`.

Else the error could also be more understandable, such as "no container registries found in configuration retrieved from keyring/configuration file at path …".
